originalGroup.material:
Paper Boat Race Test 008

For a paper-boat race, our group first chose the widest boat because it looked strong. During a test in the sink, it carried six small counters without sinking. A narrow boat carried only four. We thought the choice was easy. Then our teacher reminded us that the race would be along a shallow channel with moving water. In the channel, the wide boat kept touching the sides and stopped. The narrow boat moved farther even with a lighter load. We changed our plan. We kept the sink results in our notes, but we chose the narrow boat for the race. We did not claim that it could carry more weight; it was simply more useful for this course.

originalGroup.material:
Uniform Swap Tags 008

At the school uniform swap, families donated clean clothes they no longer needed. Volunteers checked each item and wrote its size on a plain tag. They removed old name labels before displaying the clothes. The event was free, and families could take an item even if they had nothing to donate.
The first layout grouped clothes by colour. It looked tidy, but parents had to search through several tables for one size. After an hour, volunteers regrouped them by size and added a small colour marker to each tag. This kept colour information without making it the main sorting rule. A sign said that sizes on old labels could vary, so pupils should try items on in the screened area. Volunteers counted the clothes taken, but they did not record which family needed which size.
